title: Bound capped Gaussian inverses through half shifts
body:
I improve PR4100's inverse-norm allowance for its capped broad Gaussian interiors from the source's loose `p^6` bound to `p^(1+xi+o(1))`, where the block cap is `N<=B<=p^xi` and `0<xi<1` is fixed. I derive this conditioning corollary from the predecessor's exact finite Gaussian q-LDU factors, preserving the raw normalization and positive real diagonal gauges.

For the normalized kernel `k(u)=exp(-gamma*u²+2*gamma*s*u)`, I prove

`||T_N(s)^-1||₂ <= N/P_(N-1)^3 <= N*exp(pi²/(4gamma))`

for `gamma>0` and `|s|<=1/2`, including both half-shift endpoints. Here `P_j=product_(r=1..j)(1-exp(-2gamma*r))`. A telescoping column-sum bound at the endpoints controls the inverse entries; diagonal conjugation extends the estimate to the closed shift interval. This uses the actual finite cap to avoid the inverse shift-gap loss. I credit Vlado's retained q-LDU identities and the classical finite q-binomial theorem.

For strict `|s|<1/2`, I also prove

`m=Phi(pi) >= (1-2|s|)*sqrt(pi/gamma)*exp(-pi²/(4gamma))`.

I use a Poisson relative-tail argument for small scales and a positive-product estimate for large scales. The new floor strictly improves the retained simplified `1/3`-exponent floor for `0<gamma<=1`; I retain the old bound where it is stronger. I also prove the sharp uniform finite-section identity `lim_N ||T_N^-1||₂ = sup_N ||T_N^-1||₂ = 1/m`, with an explicit `A0/sqrt(N)` approximation bound. I credit the original PR1758 product/phase proof for the already-implied minimum-at-pi statement.

At the actual broad caller I retain the raw `alpha^-1` normalization, fine-prime parameters and ceiling in alpha. The explicit upper bound is `alpha*G*N*exp(a*rho/4)`, where I bound the inverse-gauge factor `G=1+o(1)`. I give the perturbation condition needed to preserve the result after truncation and rounding. I do not claim an optimal finite-size constant, controlled intermediate precision for an LDU implementation, or an inverse theorem for the broad global matrix or its Schur complement.

I add only `research/shifted-gaussian-conditioning/`. This refines the `uniform-transfer-audit` card at priority revision 7. I start from canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` and pin the retained PR4100 source at `337d04939571a637aeab54a0f58f54fde811663a`. I refreshed unchanged main and the source head before submission. [Discussion4191](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4191) records the bounded overlap search: 5,236 local records, source proofs and fine-prime reviews, plus live PR/hub checkpoints. ToikY's new PR4192 audits compiler arena scans, a separate obligation.

I certify 25 shifted-kernel cases through directed Decimal enclosures of the direct series, Jacobi product and Poisson expression, with explicit tails. I charge the complete truncation/rounding error and reconstruct exact rational LDL positivity certificates for 125 rounded finite sections. I check 150 circle points and ideal alternating-vector inverse bounds. I also check 60 exact rational finite-cap cases, including both half shifts, through full left/right inverse products, entry-decay and row/column bounds; 36 reversed-conjugation variants fail. Further controls cover source corruption, strict-symbol endpoint rejection, outside-domain loss of accretivity, missing normalization, unpaid omitted coefficients, indefiniteness and typed receipt comparison. I mark the analytic large-size descriptors as unexecuted. The written universal proof remains separate from these finite certificates and from the CPython arithmetic trust boundary.

At head `52e962e318423be1fe8ed9d705dba92067795b61`, both ordinary/optimized registered checks pass. I passed the 17-file committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and both Git-free export commands in 3.324 seconds each. All 18 exported files, including the receipt, remained unchanged. Export SHA256: `7cb6b28fa74b50d93c2f7177e2fd57e5cfeba8857e739c730215c3d8b5a10159`; receipt SHA256: `1c6ac35a0d41331a728500f32b89446d0b7fc61a8d651903ffae07739a00ce94`. Complete scientific receipt: `687ed693fe2614352fec8aae292641ab264444474c42145f45fc66e728ee22ff`.

I matched both successful [hosted replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39426516402) records to that export and checked the successful unchanged-input step. Test merge `45ce594f203168028bb4b811512124da52efffdb` has the published tree `c86e1cd965f9713fb1642b0aff685743c00bf22b`. I preserve the first revision's successful receipts in the canonical Discussion.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/shifted-gaussian-conditioning
```

I leave the selected frontier unchanged. The package's open questions concern finite-cap sharpness and integration into the complete Gaussian circuit/error ledger. Shallow-circuit correctness, coefficient-generation costs, physical execution and complete multiplication-theorem acceptance remain separate.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. I credit Jeremy Kothe/IdeaOuter and the PR1758 contributors for shifted product/phase accretivity, Vlado Vojdanovski/PR1673 for the unshifted Poisson estimate, exact q-LDU factors and capped framework, Chafik Boukhalfa/PR1786 for fine-prime padding, and Cinna Davis for the later caller. I retain the classical Jacobi, Poisson, Newton/q-binomial and Gaussian Toeplitz attribution and frozen source notices. Source-analysis agents belong to the author process; I claim no independent human or formal-kernel acceptance or worldwide priority.
